explorer.prompt: You have L$50. A toy costs L$30 and a game costs L$40. You can't buy both. How do you choose well?
options: Pick the first thing you see, right away
Pick whichever you will enjoy most and for longest
Pick the one your friend picked
explorer.explain: Money is limited, so every choice means giving something up. Thinking about which want matters most to you, and for how long, helps you choose well.

explorer.prompt: A bike costs L$40. You save L$10 every week and spend none of it. When can you buy the bike?
options: After 2 weeks
After 10 weeks
After 4 weeks
explorer.explain: L$10 each week adds up: L$10, L$20, L$30, then L$40 after four weeks. Waiting and saving a little at a time lets you afford bigger things.

explorer.prompt: A club makes only 100 special stickers. Then it prints 1,000,000 more just like them. What usually happens to each sticker's worth?
options: It goes down, because they are no longer rare
It goes up, because there are more stickers
It stays exactly the same
explorer.explain: When something is rare, people value it more. Make lots more, and each one is worth less. That is why VAULT has a hard cap on how many can ever exist.

trader.prompt: You have L$1,000. One of your coins might suddenly crash to nearly zero. Which setup would hurt the least?
options: All L$1,000 in the one coin you like most
L$800 in one coin and L$200 kept in L$
L$300 in each of three coins, L$100 in L$
trader.explain: If one coin crashes, you only lose what you put in it. Here the most you could lose is L$300. Putting too much in one place is called concentration risk.

trader.prompt: A coin's price is steady. Twice as many people suddenly want to buy it, but the number for sale stays the same. What happens?
options: The price tends to rise
The price tends to fall
The price tends to stay the same
trader.explain: When more people want something and the supply for sale stays the same, buyers compete. That pushes the price up. This is supply and demand.

trader.prompt: Which reason for buying a coin is hype?
options: I read how its supply works and it fits
Everyone is buying it, so I must hurry
I kept some L$ aside and spread my money
trader.explain: Hype means buying because everyone else is buying. A rush like that can lift a price fast, and it usually fades just as fast. Having your own reasons keeps you steady.

builder.prompt: A coin will unlock a quarter of its locked team coins tomorrow, with the rest vesting slowly. What is the main thing to think about?
options: More coins can be sold, and some insiders may sell
Unlocked coins are destroyed, so each coin becomes rarer
Nothing changes, because those coins already existed
builder.explain: An unlock raises the circulating supply. If some insiders sell, that extra selling can push the price down. Vesting spreads the release out so it hits the market more gently.

builder.prompt: A new coin's creator holds 60% of its coins, and its pool is not locked. What does this combination mean?
options: The coin will trade more slowly but safely
The creator could pull the pool money and crash it
The creator's coins will be burned to protect holders
builder.explain: A huge creator share and an unlocked pool are both red flags. The creator could remove the money from the pool and sell, leaving holders unable to sell for anything near what they paid.

builder.prompt: A coin's trading volume spikes, but its price barely moves. The same trader appears on both sides of many trades. What is likely going on?
options: Real demand from many new buyers
The pool has been locked for safety
Wash trading, which makes volume look busy without real demand
builder.explain: Wash trading is one trader buying from and selling to itself. Volume looks busy, but there is no real demand, so the price barely moves. Busy volume alone does not prove interest.
